best_norm:
MONTHLY HARVEST RULE (v1)

1. Stock check: At the start of each month, measure current lake stock S (before fishing).
2. Hard floor: If S < 20 tons, NO fishing is allowed that month (all quotas = 0) until stock recovers above 20.
3. Catch cap: If S ≥ 20 tons, total allowable catch = 45% of S. Each of the 5 fishers may take up to 9% of S (i.e., an equal 1/5 share of the 45% total) — a fixed, non-transferable individual quota. Unused quota may not be transferred, sold, or reallocated to others that month.
4. Reporting: Each fisher must publicly report their actual catch that month before the next month's stock check. Reports and resulting stock levels are logged and visible to all.
5. Amendment rule: This norm may only be changed by a proposal stating exact new numeric percentages/thresholds (no vague language), and requires approval from at least 4 of 5 fishers. Proposals to lower the cap for extra safety are discouraged unless stock data show S repeatedly falling below 40 tons after fishing.
6. Rationale (for fishers' reference): 45% total cap leaves a buffer below the ~50% regeneration ceiling, so the stock keeps regrowing even after full harvest, avoiding collapse while capturing more yield than overly conservative (30%) caps. Equal fixed shares plus forfeiture-on-noncompliance remove incentive to cheat, and public reporting makes deviations immediately visible, sustaining trust in the rule without needing external enforcement.

trajectory.norm: Fishers should be mindful of the shared lake and avoid taking so much that the fish cannot recover. Take a reasonable, fair share.
final_norms: Each month, the total catch by all fishers combined should not exceed 30% of the fish present at the start of that month. Each fisher should aim to catch no more than 6% of the starting amount individually (so with 5 fishers, this naturally sums to ~30%). This ensures the lake can regenerate toward full carrying capacity. If the lake level is below 20 tons, no fishing is allowed that month to let it recover. All fishers must report actual catch honestly at month's end.

Each month, the total catch by all fishers combined should not exceed 40% of the fish present at the start of that month. Each fisher should aim to catch no more than 1/5 (one fifth) of that month's allowed total (i.e., 8% of the starting stock per fisher), to keep shares fair and equal. If the stock at the start of the month is below 20 tons, all fishers must stop fishing that month to let the lake recover, since going below 5 tons destroys the lake permanently.

playbook: Vague norms ("take a reasonable share") get quickly replaced (rewritten ~1.5x, first change round 0) with precise numeric rules once fishers see ambiguity invites free-riding—specific % caps are far more stable and enforceable.

Tying the catch limit to the *current* stock (e.g. "≤6% of starting amount per fisher, 30% total") plus a hard stop below a threshold (no fishing under 20 tons) reliably prevents collapse (o=0.000, 12/12 survival) and preserves equality (e=0.972), since it self-adjusts and is easy to verify/audit.

Setting the harvest cap well below the true sustainable yield (30% total vs the ~50% MSY) trades efficiency for safety—here u=0.698—so a good norm should calibrate the % cap closer to the regeneration rate (e.g. ~45-50% of stock) to raise total gain without reintroducing over-usage risk.

7. RATIONALE (for stability): 45% total keeps harvest below the ~50% regeneration rate, leaving a buffer so stock trends upward toward carrying capacity over time, increasing future yields for everyone.
